_meta.note: Tunable rule pack for the Estate-to-Target Migration Assessor. Edit thresholds here rather than in code. Every limit carries a 'source' hint so reviewers can verify against current Microsoft documentation.

SQL_VM.label: SQL Server on Azure VM
SQL_VM.shape: IaaS - full OS and instance control

SQL_DB.note: Hyperscale lifts the size ceiling; flagged as an upsell rather than a blocker.

SQL_MI.note: General Purpose and Business Critical instance ceilings.

blockers.label: Cross-database queries / three-part naming
blockers.remediation: Consolidate dependent databases onto SQL MI, or refactor to elastic query / synonyms.

blockers.label: SQL Server Agent jobs
blockers.remediation: SQL MI supports Agent natively. For SQL DB, re-host as Elastic Jobs or Azure Automation.

blockers.label: Service Broker
blockers.remediation: SQL MI supports Service Broker within the instance. SQL DB requires re-architecting onto Azure Service Bus.

blockers.label: CLR assemblies
blockers.remediation: SAFE assemblies are supported on SQL MI. UNSAFE/EXTERNAL_ACCESS assemblies require SQL on VM or code replacement.

blockers.label: Linked servers
blockers.remediation: SQL MI supports linked servers to SQL targets only. Non-SQL providers (Oracle, ODBC, Excel) require SQL on VM.

blockers.label: FileStream / FileTable
blockers.remediation: Not supported on any SQL PaaS tier. Move to SQL on VM, or re-architect onto Azure Blob Storage.

blockers.label: Database Mail / xp_cmdshell / OLE Automation
blockers.remediation: xp_cmdshell and OLE Automation are unavailable on PaaS. Database Mail is supported on SQL MI. Re-host OS-level calls as Azure Functions or Automation runbooks.

blockers.label: SSIS / SSRS / SSAS co-located on the instance
blockers.remediation: Separate the BI tier: SSIS to Azure Data Factory SSIS-IR, SSRS to Power BI Paginated Reports, SSAS to Power BI Premium or Fabric. The database engine itself can still land on PaaS.

blockers.label: Transactional replication publisher
blockers.remediation: SQL MI can act as publisher, distributor and subscriber. SQL DB can only subscribe.

blockers.label: Non-default or unsupported instance collation
blockers.remediation: SQL MI instance collation is fixed at creation and cannot be changed afterwards. Confirm the collation up front; SQL DB supports database-level collation only.

blockers.label: Deprecated or discontinued feature in use
blockers.remediation: Raise the database compatibility level and remove discontinued syntax before migration. Test with Query Store and the Database Experimentation Assistant.

blockers.label: Instance-level trace flags
blockers.remediation: Only a small subset of global trace flags is honoured on SQL MI. Validate each flag; most legacy tempdb flags are redundant on modern engines.

blockers.label: Semantic search / full-text with custom components
blockers.remediation: Standard full-text search is supported on PaaS. Semantic search and custom word breakers are not.

blockers.label: Windows authentication dependency
blockers.remediation: Map to Microsoft Entra authentication. SQL MI supports Entra-only and Kerberos via Entra Domain Services.

blockers.label: SQL Server version out of support
blockers.remediation: Out-of-support versions carry ESU cost and security exposure. PaaS targets remove the patching obligation entirely; this strengthens the migration business case.

business_critical_triggers.note: Business Critical uses local NVMe and provides a free readable replica. General Purpose is remote storage and cheaper.

non_production.note: Non-production workloads are migrated first as a low-risk proving ground, and are never sized for Business Critical. Detecting them separately stops dev databases inflating the complex waves and the run-rate.

fabric_heuristics.note: Fabric is proposed as a re-platform CANDIDATE only. It is never auto-assigned over an OLTP workload; it requires human confirmation because it changes the application contract.

S.label: Simple
S.criteria: No hard blockers, under 200 GB, supported version

M.label: Moderate
M.criteria: At most two medium findings, under 1 TB

L.label: Complex
L.criteria: Hard blocker requiring remediation, or over 1 TB

XL.label: Re-architect
XL.criteria: Multiple hard blockers, over 5 TB, or a Fabric re-platform

waves.name: Wave 1 - Quick wins
waves.intent: Prove the migration factory and bank early credit. Land these first.

waves.name: Wave 2 - Standard
waves.intent: Bulk of the estate. Repeatable runbook, minimal remediation.

waves.name: Wave 3 - Complex
waves.intent: Remediation required before cutover. Needs application-team engagement.

waves.name: Wave 4 - Re-architect
waves.intent: Design-led. Treat as a project in its own right, not a migration task.

pricing.note: Azure Hybrid Benefit can remove the SQL licence component for customers with Software Assurance. The discount hint is indicative only and must be validated per agreement.
